top_level_objectives: Identify the components and structure of a DNA molecule.
Describe the process of DNA replication, including the roles of key enzymes.
Explain the concept of semiconservative replication.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce students to the basic structure of the DNA double helix.
key_visuals: A rotating 3D model of the DNA double helix, highlighting the sugar-phosphate backbone and nitrogenous bases.
student_actions: Rotate the DNA model to view it from all angles.
Identify the sugar-phosphate backbones.
Observe the nitrogenous bases projecting inward.

scenes.brief_purpose: Illustrate the complementary base pairing rules and the role of hydrogen bonds.
key_visuals: Close-up view of adenine-thymine (A-T) base pair showing two hydrogen bonds.
Close-up view of guanine-cytosine (G-C) base pair showing three hydrogen bonds.
student_actions: Observe the A-T base pair and count the hydrogen bonds.
Observe the G-C base pair and count the hydrogen bonds.
Confirm that A pairs with T, and G pairs with C.

scenes.brief_purpose: Explain the antiparallel nature of the DNA strands and 5'/3' directionality.
key_visuals: DNA double helix model with one strand explicitly labeled 5' to 3'
Highlight the orientation of the sugar molecules.
student_actions: Identify the 5' and 3' ends of each strand.
Observe how the two strands run in opposite directions.
Relate strand directionality to the sugar-phosphate backbone.

scenes.brief_purpose: Show the unwinding of the DNA helix at the replication fork.
key_visuals: A segment of DNA helix beginning to unwind.
Animation showing helicase enzyme moving along the DNA.
student_actions: Observe the DNA helix unwinding.
Identify the helicase enzyme.
Recognize the formation of the replication fork.

scenes.scene_name: DNA Polymerase Action: Leading and Lagging Strands
scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate the synthesis of new DNA strands by DNA polymerase, highlighting leading and lagging strand synthesis.
key_visuals: Animation showing DNA polymerase synthesizing the leading strand continuously.
Animation showing DNA polymerase synthesizing the lagging strand discontinuously in Okazaki fragments.
Single-strand binding proteins stabilizing the parental strands.
student_actions: Observe the continuous synthesis of the leading strand.
Observe the discontinuous synthesis of the lagging strand.
Identify Okazaki fragments.
Note the role of single-strand binding proteins.

scenes.brief_purpose: Show DNA ligase joining Okazaki fragments and illustrate the semiconservative nature of replication.
key_visuals: Animation showing DNA ligase joining Okazaki fragments.
Two complete DNA double helix molecules formed.
Each new molecule shown to contain one original and one new strand.
student_actions: Observe DNA ligase sealing the gaps in the lagging strand.
Examine the two resulting DNA molecules.
Identify the parental and newly synthesized strands in each daughter molecule.
Confirm that each new DNA molecule is composed of one old and one new strand.
